previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, prior CABG, CVA, and chronic alcohol use was admitted after being found unconscious on the floor following heavy alcohol consumption. He reported sharp, reproducible left-sided chest pain and leg pain attributed to a fall. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal troponins and prior negative stress test; chest pain was deemed musculoskeletal. CT head and spine showed no acute abnormalities. Liver enzymes were elevated, consistent with acute alcoholic hepatitis, which improved with supportive care. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal but remained stable without symptoms. Electrolyte imbalances from dehydration resolved with IV fluids. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to reduce alcohol intake, continue cardiac and liver-protective medications, and follow up with primary care.

Discharge Instructions:
You came into the hospital with chest pain after eating a big 
meal with alcohol.  We diagnosed you with gastric reflux.  In 
the hospital, we controlled your pain with morphine and 
antacids, and gave you IV fluids and vitamins since you had been 
vomiting.  We verified that you did not have a heart attack and 
were not bleeding from anywhere in your GI tract.  We also 
arranged for you to speak with a substance abuse counsellor 
about your alcoholism and consult with specialists about your 
eating and mobility.
.
We are giving you a new antacid medication to help with your 
heartburn: Ranitidine (Zantac) 
.
Please call your PCP or return to the hospital if you cough up 
or vomit blood, if you have blood in your stools or black 
stools, if you experience severe chest pain or shortness of 
breath, if you lose consciousness, if you fall, if you have a 
seizure, or if you experience any symptoms that concern you.
